newsitem.title: EGYPT: Suez Canal says no new policy adopted towards Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Suez Canal says no new policy adopted towards Iraq.

text.p: A Suez Canal Authority official said on Wednesday the authority was not offering special discounts for Iraqi crude oil shipments through the waterway.

"The discount is for all shipments, not just Iraq. And it's not new, it's been around since the beginning of the year," Amin Zeid, director of transits, told Reuters. He said crude oil discounts were calculated using a variety of factors.

The London-based newspaper al-Hayat quoted the authority's chairman, Ahmed Fadel, as saying that the authority had offered a discount on Iraqi crude oil shipments. It gave no details about the price cuts.

The newspaper also quoted Fadel as saying the discount was intended to minimise the effects of the resumption of Iraqi exports through a Turkish pipeline under a U.N. food-for-oil deal on the canal's revenues.
It also quoted Fadel as saying the authority had adopted a new policy of discount on any shipments that economic studies proved feasible.
